must: Keep all existing Czech statistics tab labels and their behavior.
Preserve the dark statistics surfaces, responsive overflow, keyboard navigation, and reduced-motion behavior.
avoid: Do not add theme switching or demo-page structure to the statistics module.
Do not use glow effects that reduce label contrast.

decisions: 2026-10-11 dashboard Carousel aligned to Settings landing: Supersede the rejected cylindrical ring with the actual Settings wrapped coverflow fan, preserving manual endless first/last navigation. Reuse its 1500/1300px perspectives, distance-based9px vertical and118px depth offsets,11deg tilt, .095 scale, opacity/brightness attenuation, 700ms easing, 24px corners, thin outlines, navy side surfaces and status-accent-to-dark vertical center gradient. Side arrows sit at the card midpoint; compact accessible44px room dots replace the full-width label strip. Clinical cards keep a260px width and440px height minimum, lighter complete titles, transparent actual status circles, recorded minutes, real specialties/notices/acute evidence and original callbacks. Fade tucked-under side titles and suppress their detail-only text until selected for legibility. Guard all controls until the selected card settles, including removal fallback; clipping cannot scroll the centered stage on focus. A measured ResizeObserver fallback allows vertical scrolling before real long content touches the stationary header or wrapped selector. Settings itself, Cards/3D, mobile/Cliniq, background, permissions, data and clinical state are unchanged. No autoplay, new dependency or backend change.

2026-10-11 Circular dashboard Carousel: Supersede only the bounded horizontal scroll-snap arrangement with a real CSS3D ring. Place each existing portrait glass card on the circumference and rotate the ring manually with unbounded logical turns, so first/last join in either direction without a reverse lap. Direct room choices take the shortest route. Keep the front card full-size and centered, receding neighbors translucent with the existing edge fade, actual transparent status-ring centers, hospital colors and clinical data. One DOM card per real room; inactive cards are inert/disabled and their overlays select only. All clinical/detail controls are gated during rotation until the transform settles, with instant reduced-motion/hidden handling; horizontal drags cancel synthetic clicks and a drag on a clinical button never mutates state. Retain arrows, Home/End, all-room quick selection, deliberate horizontal trackpad gestures and native vertical scrolling. No autoplay, new library, backend or permission change; original Cards/3D/phone/Cliniq presentations remain unchanged.

2026-10-10 Third dashboard view: Add the user-selected Carousel beside the existing Cards and permission-gated 3D disposition, persisted independently per hospital. Use a non-autoplay native scroll-snap row of delicate portrait navy glass cards: full real names and phases, a transparent completed-cycle center with a fine actual-status gradient ring and rim-only halo, two recorded whole-minute timings, real AM/PM specialties, acute evidence and existing detail/emergency/lock handlers. Keep emergency-over-lock-over-pause priority, approved red/amber neon controls, original grid, shared page heading/background and clinical data authoritative. Center the selected card with quiet scaling and outer fade; provide 44px bounded arrows, keyboard Left/Right/Home/End, focus reveal and a wrapping selector for every actual room. Preserve the established phone overview and optional Cliniq design below768px; Carousel is the additional desktop/tablet presentation. No invented room names, measurements, autoplay, new dependencies, backend or clinical changes.

2026-10-10 Desktop dashboard card polish: Use a restrained presentation-only adapter at min-width768px, scoped to dashboard-cards-layout and dashboard-workspace-card. Reuse the established blue-grey palette and asymmetric SVG silhouette with a lighter uniform5% translucent surface, fine neutral outline and matching pointer/keyboard feedback. Soften title/count typography to500, improve secondary-label contrast and simplify the AM/PM band to one quiet surface with transparent slots and a thin divider. Neutral staff accents exclude emergency, lock and pause colors. Preserve the transparent status-ring centers, actual clinical colors/counts, approved neon corner controls, responsive sizes/pocket clearances, acute evidence, original mobile/Cliniq designs and all clinical handlers. No gradient, texture, decorative animation, dependency, layout, database or permission change. Reduced motion disables the outline transition with matching specificity.

2026-10-10 Settings 3D editor alignment: Reuse ModulePageHeading and the existing Management/Notifications visual contract: separate mb-7 heading, restrained 12px transparent commandbar, labelled 44px action buttons with 8px corners, cyan project-token selection and visible saved/dirty/error status. Scope a CSS adapter to spatial-settings-module; retain the global canvas/sidebar and the actual model/viewer, five original handlers, confirmation, revision guards, room bindings and persistence. Use neutral panels, fine borders, shared typography and form/focus colors instead of yellow actions, opaque bespoke panels or hover movement. Respond to available module width with three desktop columns, a bounded 600px scene plus full-width inspector on tablets, and a bounded 640px scene followed by all editing panels on phones. An outer named inline-size container controls frame auto-height with its border allowance, preventing breakpoint clipping and canvas ResizeObserver feedback. Preserve reduced motion with matching-specificity selectors, loading/empty states and accessible overflow; no dependency, data, geometry or clinical changes.

2026-10-09 Performance circular loading: Restore a restrained transparent-center SVG progress ring in Statistics Performance, with whole percentage inside and actual fetched/total history records below. Reuse the existing statistics surface, cyan performance token, 12px radius and light/dark mobile overrides. Derive progress only from the existing hospital-scoped paginated history observer, never elapsed time; unknown/zero incomplete totals remain indeterminate, incomplete full pages cap at99, and only explicit completion reaches100. Label any remaining workflow-configuration wait separately from completed history. Initial loading does not expose partial metrics; refresh uses a compact44px ring while preserving existing five boxes and delaying report readiness. Errors take precedence, motion respects reduced-motion, no artificial loading delay or new dependencies, timers, queries, backend or clinical changes.

2026-10-09 statistics navigation alignment: The desktop Statistics menu matches the accepted Acute/management commandbar rather than its former dense uppercase navigation. Keep the existing 12px neutral outer rail and icons; use the same 8px inner segment, 2px inset, 6px tab corners, 44px targets, 11px medium sentence-case labels and token-based cyan active tint. Period and print/PDF/CSV controls use matching geometry, while the fixed 224px period slot stays 50px high for both standard periods and the Performance twelve-month caption to prevent navigation shifts. Preserve all eight Czech tab labels, horizontal overflow/reveal, arrow/Home/End behavior, native focus, shared heading, sidebar, mobile UI, charts, data, filters and report handlers. Scope the adapter to statistics-desktop, reuse current tokens and components, with no dependency, backend or clinical change.

2026-10-09 acute day workspace: Align the Acute module with Management/Notifications using the shared stationary heading, compact neutral 12px KPI/tab/action commandbar and restrained transparent content surfaces. Preserve the approved urgency-gradient request cards, global canvas, sidebar and Timeline dialogs. Reuse Statistics DayNavigator and GlassCalendar in a 280px right rail on wide desktop, stacking accessibly below content on narrower viewports. Requests and the circular timeline default to today's Europe/Prague calendar day and filter by immutable receivedAt; other-day waiting/begun requests remain visible in History with an explicit waiting-count notice. History retains actual performed-cycle evidence, archived requests, audit and existing 30/90/365-day choices. Missing historical receipt dates use actual cycle start only with explicit disclosure, never inferred receipt counts or invented calendar activity. A shared read query covers the union of history and selected day; retain full binding evidence and full queue reorder payloads. Clamp the 365-day picker window safely across midnight and keep the live clock independent of selected date; new requests always use the real current receipt time. Preserve hospital scoping, permissions, manual order, clinical callbacks and mobile light/dark tokens. No dependency, migration, external project export or clinical write.

2026-10-09 main Timeline acute toolbar tile: Replace the desktop standalone acute-count/open/caveat strip with one compact navigation-only Akutni pozadavky tile immediately beside ARO status. Both existing ARO branches and the new control share equal-width 48px geometry, neutral translucent surfaces and semantic icons/text; narrow desktop places the pair together on a second commandbar row to avoid the clock. Show the actual shared waiting projection, explicit loading/error rather than false zero, and an accessible unassigned count. Native button invokes only existing module navigation; no fetching, clinical writes, data or authorization changes. Preserve module/role gates, acute estimate semantics and the mobile summary, where no ARO toolbar tile exists.

2026-10-09 acute timeline completed vertical boxes: Supersede the lower horizontal completed strip with a single full-width column of compact performed-procedure boxes at every viewport, without fixed auto-columns or sideways scrolling. Retain 76px transparent urgency rings, actual room/procedure names, original entry number, recorded completion/wait/cycle times and chronology. Reuse the acute module's subtle card surface, 12px corners, fine border and semantic left accent. Wide layouts align identity, completion time and evidence within each row; narrow layouts wrap these inside the same box. Preserve large waiting/begun timeline layout, existing native detail buttons, focus behavior, filters and clinical/data state.

2026-10-09 acute requests waiting first: In the Requests tab, show the waiting heading and existing cards first, begun cycles second, and performed cycles below them. Preserve the manually managed waiting queue, current card appearance, actual cycle evidence and detail callbacks. When no requests wait, the honest no-waiting context remains first and completed history stays visible below it. Timeline and History tabs, styling, clinical state and data are unchanged.

2026-10-09 acute timeline completed strip: The user's correction separates completed procedures from the large active timeline. Keep waiting and begun nodes as the existing transparent large circles with live whole-minute waiting; show performed cycles only in a compact lower band with 76px transparent urgency-colored circles, checks, full procedure and actual room names, original entry number, actual completion time and recorded durations. Preserve chronology within each group, existing period filters, actual completion evidence and detail/focus callbacks. The lower band remains horizontal with local overflow on phone, while active nodes retain the accepted mobile vertical flow. Hide an empty completed band; completed-only history keeps a short honest no-active context. Reuse the existing ring SVG and theme tokens, without new dependencies or clinical/data changes.

2026-10-09 acute circular timeline: Replace only the Acute module's text-only time tab with an open-canvas connected series of transparent concentric circles. Waiting circles show whole receipt-to-cycle-start minutes inside; begun cycles use a clock and explicit Cyklus zahajen, completed cycles use a check and Provedeno based on actual immutable end evidence. Preserve urgency rose/green/ice-blue from existing tokens, actual room names, original entry number separate from current rank, frozen cycle identity and recorded whole-cycle duration. Each dated node is chronologically anchored to receipt, actual start or actual end respectively; spacing is explicitly schematic, never a progress percentage or clinical deadline. Include unassigned waiting and cycles without archived request snapshots. Desktop is an internally scrollable horizontal axis; phone is a continuous vertical sequence without page-width overflow. Reuse the existing static phase-ring pattern and Timeline/Radix detail callbacks, no new dependencies, clinical writes or external project export. All data remains gated by the existing scoped shared sources and error/loading states.

2026-10-09 acute module completed-cycle evidence: Keep the accepted urgency-gradient cards, shared module heading and canonical Timeline dialog shell. Separate unbound waiting requests, begun recorded cycles and Provedené výkony; Provedeno requires durable end time plus end-event evidence for the entire room cycle including cleanup. Completed cards and details use frozen procedure, urgency, original submission number, actual room and actual start/end/full-cycle rounded minutes, not the mutable proposal or manual request status. Read historical links directly with explicit 30/90/365-day periods, independently of the bounded request audit snapshot; retain bindings for still-open requests outside the period. Stop waiting at recorded start, preserve manual queue closure/reordering and clinical handlers, and never invent completion when evidence loading fails. Reuse existing project primitives without external export, new dependencies or clinical writes.

2026-10-08 acute queue selection and dashboard evidence: Opening a non-head unbound request keeps the complete real waiting queue, including skipped predecessors and the selected request. Use the accepted borderless room ribbon, a restrained semantic warning accent and explicit 'Není dodrženo pořadí výkonů', with current operational rank distinct from the immutable entry number. Highlight and reveal the selected queue node without changing clinical state, rank or page scroll. A bound cycle does not imply a historical order violation. Dashboard cards receive one shared authorized read-only room map: a compact urgency-tinted passive label identifies the real assigned pending procedure/current rank/count or an exactly bound running acute cycle. Complete binding evidence excludes already-performed requests even outside the Timeline window. Preserve configured phase colors, transparent gauge centers, action pockets and mobile themes. Reserve extra card height uniformly across the grid, not only on acute cards; no hidden rooms or new dependency. Reuse current 21st-informed primitives without external project export or clinical writes.

2026-10-08 durable acute cycle marking: Explicit confirmed ready-to-arrival binds a selected request atomically to the real room cycle. A completed actual Timeline block carries a compact neutral glass label '#N · Akutní · procedure' with one semantic urgency dot and frozen submission metadata; narrow desktop/mobile blocks compact the text without widening the real recorded duration. Keep actual phase colors, all room rows, whole-cycle statistics clicks and the accepted borderless room queue ribbon unchanged. RoomDetail only claims running/completed after durable evidence; a selected request opened during an unrelated running cycle is clearly labelled for the next cycle. Reuse existing tokens, no new dependencies, no generated demo clinical data. Merely opening is still navigation-only; this supersedes only the earlier limitation that no persistent cycle association exists.

2026-10-08 acute room ribbon alignment, superseding its rejected framed navy shell: The queue belongs directly to RoomDetail's open phase canvas. Remove the outer filled panel, border, blur, inset shadow and selected tinted block. Selected procedure uses the room detail's lighter typography at 20–26px; following titles are 15px and supporting labels 11–12px. Following request controls reuse the existing room-action glass language: neutral white at approximately 5% opacity, a 10% hairline border and 16px corners, with a thin connector only between adjacent controls. Keep one fine selected/queue divider, restrained urgency dots/text, original submission number and current queue rank as distinct labels. Avoid nested navy surfaces or decorative glow. Mobile controls use the existing m-card/m-border text/theme tokens, and long room labels wrap alongside estimates instead of overflowing. Preserve positioning between heading and circles, all request content, navigation, focus, actual room identities and clinical callbacks; only the component-local stylesheet and its design regression tests change.

2026-10-08 acute Timeline square label correction: Per the user's annotated screenshot, urgency tint fills the complete room-name-column cell, with zero outer margins and zero corner radius. Its left edge is a straight full-height 3px semantic urgency stripe. Preserve the gentle palette/gradient, original-entry badge, readable text, time-block appearance and all projection/data behavior. Apply the same full-cell geometry on mobile without changing phone themes; this supersedes the inset rounded label only.

2026-10-08 acute Timeline entry number: Add a small theme-aware urgency-tinted number badge to each left request label and repeat the number inside its time block, including narrow blocks and mobile. Label it Pořadí při zápisu, not clinical priority or current queue rank. The server reads the immutable create audit's new_position and retrieves missing older create entries in tenant-scoped 100-id batches; never infer a number from a reordered queue, visible-room order or clipped window. Missing evidence shows an honest dash. Preserve the approved full-height surfaces, receipt times, real duration widths, focus, actual cycles and statistics; reuse existing 21st primitives with no database write or migration.

2026-10-08 acute Timeline lane polish: Request labels in the room-name column use a gentle urgency-tinted 8px surface, a thin semantic side accent and brighter neutral text. Emergent remains rose, urgent is green, expedited is sky blue. Replace the rejected narrow dashed/hatched block with a clean lightly graded 6px block stretched over the full existing 44px request row, labelled Odhad and the recorded minutes. Container queries compact text rather than widening the recorded time span. Preserve receipt anchoring, clipping, separate overlapping request rows, mobile dark/light text tokens, keyboard focus, actual phases and statistics. Reuse the application's Timeline primitives without new dependencies or clinical writes; this supersedes the previous dashed acute request appearance only.

2026-10-08 acute Timeline receipt anchoring: Desktop and mobile dashed request lanes now start at the persisted server receivedAt, not an optional proposedStartAt or the moving current clock. Show the receipt time and surgical-only estimate in the existing 44px lane, clearly distinct from recorded surgery, reservation and occupancy. Keep exact recorded timestamps, duration clipping, independent overlapping lanes, explicit clinical urgency, module/permission gating and all actual statistics unchanged. Acute module's timeline list uses the same receipt order; only requests without rooms remain unassigned. Existing metadata and history are preserved, without migration or clinical mutations. Reuse current 21st-informed Timeline primitives, tokens and accessible sibling controls.

The October 3 mobile Timeline supersedes room pagination with an ultraminimal continuous schedule: all rooms render together, compact 32px-minimum rows align a two-line room-name rail with a thin phase track, a configured current-phase dot and stacked team dots. Remove summary cards, repeated phase captions and visible unused-minute chips; preserve their accessible descriptions and existing room-detail access. Keep the shared time ruler, 2h/4h/day windows, Now and 44px time controls, semantic actual/estimate/pause treatments and navy/light tokens. Short displays and exceptionally long room lists scroll vertically inside the schedule instead of hiding rooms. Desktop layout, clinical data, calculations and handlers are unchanged. Existing MobileShell primitives are retained; catalog scheduler matches were considered but did not justify new dependencies.

Speed diagnostics inside System Settings shares its existing translucent surfaces, 16px inner panels, fine borders, compact heading, neutral metric cards and blue pill primary action. Remove the separate opaque teal canvas, decorative grid, circular gauge and recommendation glow; show running progress as a thin labelled bar and completed quality as a compact score and semantic badge. Use the actual panel width to stack metric cards. Keep all probes, timeout handling, calculations, recommendations and permissions unchanged; sample bars represent each recorded sample once and the empty state contains no simulated data.

System Settings now adopts the user-supplied October 3 glass workspace reference, superseding its older compact horizontal rail: a soft translucent 24px shell, a local section list with framed icons, descriptive labels and a quiet blue-violet selected row, real configuration metrics, and a separated working panel with fine borders and rounded form controls. Blue pill primary and ghost secondary actions stay restrained without particles or decorative animation. Keep the outer application sidebar, shared page heading, original background, section permissions, data handlers and confirmation dialogs unchanged. Stack the workspace at narrow widths; keep every section and metric available, 44px form targets, labelled fields and reduced-motion support. No reference photo, chat content or external dependencies are imported.

Dashboard emergency and lock buttons use matching subtle neon hover and active states with white icons: a bright thin red or amber outline, an 8%-opacity tint, the approved tight exterior halo, and a visible feathered inner glow with a brighter inner rim replace the rejected opaque fill. Active glow remains after pointer exit; inactive appearance, button geometry, the transparent cycle-count center and operational handlers stay unchanged.

Responsive room cards retain at least 320px width and 44px-minimum circular action targets with at least 4px clearance between buttons and from the curved SVG pocket. The controls scale gently with card width and do not translate on hover. The grid recalculates on resize/orientation changes and uses vertical scrolling when all readable cards cannot fit; no rooms are hidden or squeezed. Below 768px the established phone overview remains authoritative, with unchanged phase colors and transparent desktop cycle centers.

The October desktop dashboard refinement preserves the existing asymmetric room-card grid, all operational content, configured status colors and page background. Stronger secondary-label contrast, slightly larger height-aware cycle indicators, cleaner specialty bands and static hover/focus emphasis improve readability without moving cards. The cycle number sits inside a fully transparent circle with no inner fill or central glow; a faint configured-status halo follows only the circumference. Mobile, room detail, data calculations and clinical actions remain unchanged.

Performance statistics follows the Phases tab: a 280px left rail with a single continuous summary (no nested metric tiles) and a separate filter panel; fluid main column with indicators and trend; full-width evidence and monthly table below. Keep the statistics command bar's period slot at the same width and height for Performance and other tabs, so labels, exports and content do not shift on selection. Neutral surfaces, 12px desktop panel corners, compact headings, framed icons, preserved measurements and original application background.

Authenticated desktop page headings share the dashboard contract: 128px left and 40px right gutters, 40px top inset, centered 2400px content limit, 23–64px fluid title based on (viewport minus the shared gutters) × .036, and an 8–11px kicker with .22em tracking. Titles are approximately another 10% smaller than the previous 25–72px scale, with unchanged placement. Heading copy stays top-aligned even with taller actions. Dashboard cards/3D, Settings carousel/grid and nested modules, Statistics tabs, Patient Flow, Alerts and room detail retain identical title coordinates. The desktop Timeline is an explicit exception: no page title or kicker above its existing commandbar. Mobile iOS headings and clinical/data handlers are unchanged.

Mobile room detail adapts to available height with container queries: compact toolbar, inline 44px estimate controls, side-by-side personnel and four actions in one row. Short landscape uses two columns and a normal-flow next-phase action, avoiding content overlays. Existing navy/light surfaces and configured status colors remain. Secondary captions compact before essential controls; exceptional content and accessibility enlargement retain an overflow fallback. Desktop and clinical handlers are unchanged.

The mobile Rozpis module is a viewport-fitted iOS-style timeline rather than a vertically scrolling room-card list. It reuses the shared navy/light surfaces and segmented controls, offers 2-hour, 4-hour and operational-day windows plus a Now action, and paginates rooms according to measured available height. Actual recorded phases use solid semantic colors, future estimates are dashed, pauses are striped, and empty windows explicitly say no record rather than implying room availability. Short screens reduce supplementary summary/header content while preserving 44px navigation controls and room-detail access. Desktop scheduling, backend reads/writes and clinical workflow handlers remain unchanged.

The 2026-09-17 mobile room overview uses two equal-width iOS-inspired tiles per row, replacing the previous full-width room rows. It retains shared navy/light surfaces, 20px corner radius, 16px title inset and 17px semibold headings. Full room names wrap without truncation; semantic phase text/dots sit beneath them, two labelled times follow, and a separate 44px footer keeps detail navigation and contextual actions accessible. Search, filters, live status data, permissions and the desktop layout remain unchanged.

Phone cards follow one surface contract across room overview/detail, patient flow, timeline, spatial selection, statistics, personnel and the Settings landing: 20px radius, 16px internal inset, sentence-case 17px/600 title first and left-aligned. Shared page headings are 28px/700 directly in the top 44px-minimum toolbar beside actions, with 20px page gutters; introductory kickers are omitted and optional hospital/date metadata stays below. This supersedes the older mobile-specific card geometry; desktop and print stay unchanged. Dark phone surfaces use the Alerts navy-blue family (#050D2D background, #131F49 cards, #192A56 secondary surface, #88ADFF controls), with no teal structural cast. Clinical phase colors and yellow primary actions keep their existing meaning; decorative per-card fills are removed.

The 2026-09-18 mobile room-detail current phase is the semantic exception to neutral cards: use its configured live color for a vivid feathered gradient, fine outline, restrained glow, elapsed-time accent and completed/current markers. Dark mode deepens the navy center; light mode uses a pale colored surface with dark readable text. The top row holds the current-phase label and actual enabled-workflow position/count. Ready stays neutral; pause, emergency and lock retain existing priority colors. Preserve shared card geometry, the real workflow rail, confirmations and all clinical handlers. No hardcoded surgery pink or reference-specific step count.

The 2026-09-17 iOS refinement follows Apple Design Resources and HIG patterns while retaining the approved apka.jpg palette: system-first phone typography, large sentence-case titles, grouped inset room/personnel lists, neutral raised segmented controls, restrained separators, and a translucent bottom tab bar with an accessible More sheet. Yellow remains reserved for primary actions and dark active navigation; configured phase colors retain their operational meaning. The detail keeps all four clinical actions and its 15-minute estimate stepper with at least 44px targets. Styles are phone-only through 767px; desktop, actual spatial geometry/materials, permissions, workflow handlers, confirmations, and data access remain unchanged. This is an iOS-inspired React/Capacitor interface, not a SwiftUI rewrite or a claim of pixel fidelity to the supplied empty Figma canvas.

The 2026-09-15 apka.jpg reference supersedes the earlier mobile canvas choices for the phone dashboard and room detail only: delicate ice-blue/white light surfaces and restrained deep-navy dark surfaces, hairline borders, compact typography, semantic phase dots, and yellow primary actions. Phone room cards are compact searchable rows without logos; the 3D/plan view preserves the actual architectural model and uses a two-metric selected-room sheet. The detail uses a rectangular current-phase panel with the actual horizontally scrollable workflow, two ARO personnel roles, persistent Pause/Hygiene/Call/Arrival actions, and estimated-end minus/plus controls in 15-minute increments. Existing handlers, confirmations, permissions, configured phase colors, desktop layouts, and real-time data remain authoritative. Bottom navigation and the detail CTA respect safe areas and small dynamic viewport heights.
Statistics navigation uses a restrained icon-and-label glow menu with a 3D hover transition, persistent active state, horizontal mobile scrolling, and the original Czech tab names.
Individual statistics tab buttons have no visible outline; selection is communicated by color, background tint, icon, and a short bottom indicator.

Distribution cards in Finance, Rooms, Phases, Notifications, and Devices share the Finance card pattern: cyan eyebrow and top rule, 24px semibold title, 11px subtitle, compact uppercase badge, 132px segmented ring, and a compact legend.
The Rooms tab prioritizes actionable improvement insights in the main column and places the shared heat calendar directly below the operating-room summary in the sidebar.

Authenticated modules share the Settings landing-page background and header typography. The shared blue-violet application gradient is deliberately deepened slightly for stronger contrast, while the operating-room detail intentionally preserves its own phase-driven background.
The Settings carousel is centered in the full viewport; its central card always shows a unique per-module accent that appears at the top and blends smoothly into the dark surface toward the bottom.
Application backgrounds are fixed CSS surfaces; the former background/design settings module, runtime background configuration, image backgrounds, and decorative background animation are removed.

The operating-room schedule uses the same restrained dark surfaces, compact KPI hierarchy, typography, borders, and cyan accents as Statistics → Rooms; its summary metrics and planning-period controls form one uninterrupted horizontal row with overflow access on narrow screens while preserving week, month, year, assignment, repetition, and database behaviors.

The Settings hub is constrained to the available application viewport without page scrolling; its carousel scales with viewport height, its page heading remains outside the gesture layer and stationary, while long selected administration modules scroll only inside their content area.

The operating-room schedule marks Czech public holidays with a restrained amber accent in week, month, and year views and repeats the holiday name in the assignment dialog without blocking exceptional scheduling.

Settings → Operating rooms mirrors the operating-room schedule as a continuous management table: one horizontal KPI/action rail, gapless room rows, a fixed identity column, a today column, a seven-day operating grid, and compact row actions separated by hairline dividers. Nested room cards are omitted; compact mode reduces row height without changing structure, dialogs use the shared 12px geometry, and cyan remains reserved for active state and primary actions.

System Settings reuses the operating-room schedule shell: metrics and section navigation share one compact horizontal bar, panels use neutral transparent surfaces with 12px radii and thin white separators, and color is reserved for icons and active controls without decorative top lines or glow.

The live dashboard preserves its established room-card layout and central completed-cycle count, but adopts the Settings modules' restrained 12px glass surfaces, compact spacing, lighter borders and shadows, static semantic accents, and denser responsive grid; emergency and lock colors remain operational signals.

Each dashboard room card shows the current day's schedule as two equal AM/PM specialty fields in place of the phase-status strip; full-day assignments repeat across both fields and no leading status dot is used.

The dashboard header keeps the module heading and live clock on one row from tablet widths upward; the desktop sidebar scales button height, spacing, corner radius, and icon size against viewport height so every authorized navigation action remains visible without overlap.

Desktop operating-room cards use the reference's exact normalized 980×750 non-convex outline: a convex r=76 arc and tangent concave r=78 arc meet at x=682, the control is centered at x=760/y=76, and the lower shoulder begins at y=154. Container-width units preserve circular curvature on responsive cards; operational color remains limited to state, alerts, and progress.

Dashboard room cards use one uniform transparent fill without gradients, texture, grid, or banding and trace the complete irregular silhouette with a subtle alpha-aware outline. The S-shaped wave is vertically mirrored into the lower-right corner and holds two adjacent circular emergency and lock actions; the former upper-right room-number and detail circles are removed so the full room name remains unobstructed. The central completed-cycle number changes to an exclamation icon during Emergency and a lock icon while the room is locked, with Emergency taking visual priority if both states occur.

Timeline mirrors the Patient Flow module's open-canvas visual language while preserving its existing scheduler layout: the scheduler shell, room lanes, alternating lanes, filter header, and complete 7–23 hour header have no fill and sit directly on the shared application background. Fine structural dividers remain; completed phase fills use the Patient Flow module's low-alpha color treatment with independent high-contrast labels, while the sticky room-name rail is isolated as a slightly deeper continuous navy plane with a fine right divider and restrained edge shadow.

The timeline follows a restrained clinical-scheduler hierarchy: one contiguous schedule table, compact controls and hour axis, subtle alternating lanes, low-noise free-room badges, and a single shared working-hours label; color is reserved for operations, current time, and alerts.

The room-detail staff picker is an integrated split clinical console: a dark blurred application backdrop, the shared app-module blue-violet surface, a fixed current-assignment context column mirroring Timeline room labels, and a contiguous searchable personnel table with 12px outer radius, 6–8px controls, restrained role accents, and immediately legible free, assigned, and unavailable states.

Every Timeline modal uses one canonical clinical shell: the application-gradient blurred backdrop, an elevated blue-violet panel, 12px outer radius, 8px nested surfaces, thin dividers, compact header typography, and a consistent close control; semantic colors remain reserved for data and operational state.

Timeline modal content uses a continuous blue-violet clinical canvas. The room-cycle detail applies a restrained MotionSites-inspired editorial hierarchy: oversized progress typography, a pill eyebrow, subtle directional light, and a continuous horizontal phase rail without dark nested cards or expensive motion. Recommendations and personnel/time data remain open bands rather than nested cards.

Settings → Operating specialties uses the schedule module's compact continuous-table language: restrained transparent surfaces, thin row dividers, 12px outer radii, semantic specialty colors, stable database identities, and deactivation instead of deletion whenever schedule history exists.

The operating-room schedule assignment modal reuses the room-detail staff picker's canonical clinical shell: blurred dark application backdrop, blue-violet elevated canvas, context bar, continuous gap-pixel option grids, compact footer actions, and 12px outer geometry. Specialty accents are functional identifiers loaded from each hospital's persisted department accent_color.

Operating specialties own a required 2–10 character, dot-free hospital-unique short code. Schedule cells mirror the assignment dialog's specialty tiles with a left-aligned short code, complete specialty name, persisted color surface, and thin light separator instead of a centered code, circular marker, or colored outline. In the assignment dialog, day-part and room-state controls share one horizontal row, the full-width specialty selector uses the same contiguous segmented language as assignment validity while retaining stronger persisted colors and complete names, and the day part defaults to the full day.

Timeline room labels are transparent and split into two clear zones: the full room name may wrap naturally to two compact lines above its tiny muted description on the left, while one fixed 92px compact two-column schedule table sits on the right. Its header reads DOPOL./ODPOL.; its lower cells show hospital-defined specialty abbreviations with a nearly transparent persisted-color tint and hairline bottom accent. Full-day assignments repeat in both columns and empty positions use a neutral dash.

Settings → Calendar is a read-only operational projection of the persisted room schedule, not a second planning source. It reuses the schedule module's compact summary rail, 12px continuous calendar table, subtle dividers, persisted specialty colors, Czech-holiday accents, room filtering, and an AM/PM day-detail table; edits remain centralized in Room Schedule. Every month cell groups assignments by operating room: matching AM and PM assignments merge into one full-day band, while different assignments remain two clearly separated color-coded halves.

The live dashboard offers a persisted per-hospital choice between its established room-card grid and a lazy-loaded spatial view. Settings includes a hospital-scoped 3D layout editor derived from the supplied ORMS spatial model. Its three-panel workspace, JSON/GLB interchange, room externalId links, validation, revision-safe database persistence, and WebGL-to-2D fallback are visually wrapped in the same compact transparent blue surfaces and fine separators as the schedule and settings modules.

When the persisted dashboard view is 3D, it keeps exactly the same shared top-level OPERAČNÍ SÁLY heading, view switcher, date, and live clock as the card view. Beneath it, the operating-block cockpit remains interactive: the spatial model dominates the left stage, a selected room stays yellow-highlighted with a persistent detail panel on the right, and a bottom command strip combines hospital metrics, the real daily program, and the highest-priority operational notice. The deep navy spatial canvas belongs to the full dashboard module rather than an inset rounded container; the cockpit itself is borderless and transparent.

The 3D dashboard background follows the approved 2026-09-09 reference palette: an edge-to-edge #050d30 to #030a2c navy field with no magenta cast, a broad blue-violet ambient halo centered behind the room model, and a softer contact glow beneath the rooms. Both glows must feather to transparent before their layout boundaries so no rectangular veil or clipped edge is visible.

The spatial operating block uses one continuous architectural wall system instead of isolated room boxes: substantial matte blue-gray wall panels, restrained lighter coping, a dark structural plinth, closed inset corridor doors, high far walls and cutaway near facades. Adjacent default rooms share a wall axis without bright gaps. The selected room shifts the same wall materials to a warm neutral surface with yellow coping and floor-edge light, matching the approved reference without changing room data or interaction.

The approved 3D-disposition background is the global dark application canvas: every authenticated desktop module, the dark mobile shell, login base, and operating-room detail base reuse the same edge-to-edge navy gradient and centered ambient blue halo. Module-specific semantic glows may layer above it, but no screen introduces a separate purple or magenta page gradient.

The 3D operating block has no DOM-sized glow or blurred rectangular stage overlay. Its only model-specific blue halo is a low-opacity feathered WebGL perimeter mesh attached to the building group, fully transparent before its plane boundary, so it follows orbit rotation, plan view, pan and zoom without revealing a static box.

Statistics and all seven sections (Overview, Finance, Rates, Rooms, Phases, Notifications, Devices) reuse the interior Settings modules' management style, not the Settings landing carousel: neutral low-alpha surfaces, 12px outer panels, 8px nested surfaces, hairline separators, compact typography, and a single segmented navigation/period/export rail. Cyan denotes the active tab, while chart, phase, and alert colors retain their data meaning. Decorative glow, top stripes, pulse, and orbit-hover scaling are omitted. Tabs support arrow/Home/End keyboard navigation; narrow screens retain horizontal access without page overflow, and light mobile dialogs keep a light solid surface. Data, calculations, permissions, filters, and rate editing remain unchanged.

Statistics print and PDF use a standalone paper-first A4 report of only the selected tab and its current filters. White paper, dark navy text, restrained teal section numbering, compact metric bands, complete semantic tables with repeating headers, and page counters replace interactive dashboard graphics. Reports state the hospital, time period, selected operational day, generation time, and any narrower data scope. Export uses existing loaded data without mounting other tabs or initiating new fetches; no screen-height clipping, dark application styles, animations, hidden labels, abbreviated currency, or top-N row truncation may leak into the report. Cancelling print preserves the preview for retry; Ctrl/Cmd+P in Statistics opens the same report.
